description: A research team preparing a paper needs to keep the manuscript, appendix, code release notes, data statement, and presentation materials aligned as small edits continue across all of them.

user_profile.persona: 31-year-old postdoc coordinating the final submission package
user_profile.context: The science is done, but version drift between materials is becoming the main risk
user_profile.communication_style: Detail-oriented and consistency-driven, notices mismatches quickly

fact_sheet.fact: The manuscript is titled 'Quantum Entanglement in Cepheid Variable Analogs' for Project Stellara.
The target journal for submission is the 'Journal of Astrophysical Dynamics'.
The final submission deadline is October 25, 2024, at 5:00 PM EST.
The manuscript's submission portal tracking ID is JAD-2024-8817.
Dr. Aris Thorne is the coordinating author responsible for assembling the final submission package.
The Principal Investigator, Dr. Lena Petrova, must give final approval on all submission materials.
Dr. Kenji Tanaka is responsible for the final code package and its release notes.
Samira El-Amin is the lead for the dataset, its documentation, and the data availability statement.
The main manuscript is edited in an Overleaf project with URL: https://www.overleaf.com/project/671b9f3d4e5c6a7b8d9e0f1a.
The current working version of the manuscript and appendix is v3.1.2, tagged in Overleaf history on October 15, 2024.
The presentation slides for conferences are stored in a shared Dropbox folder named 'Stellara_JAD_Submission/Presentation'.
The presentation slide deck file is named 'Stellara_Presentation_v2.4.pptx'.
The data availability statement is a standalone document named 'DataStatement_v1.3.docx' located in the root of the Dropbox folder.
The project's code is hosted in a private Git repository at git.nit.edu/stellara/cepheid-q-sim.git.
The primary branch for the submission release is named 'submission-v1.2'.
The final, tagged version of the code for release is 'v1.2.0-final'.
The 'CODE_RELEASE_NOTES.md' file corresponds to code version 'v1.2.0-final'.
The Docker container for reproducing results is specified in the 'Dockerfile' located in the repository root.
The final dataset is stored on the Northwood Institute of Technology's 'Orion' cluster.
The full path to the final dataset directory is /data/orion/projects/stellara/final_dataset_v4/.
The dataset is archived as a single file named 'stellara_dataset_v4.tar.gz' with a SHA256 checksum of 'a3f8e5b1...c9d0'.
The public access DOI for the dataset will be provided by the Zenodo repository upon upload, with placeholder '10.5281/zenodo.XXXXXXX' used in the manuscript.
All submission-related discussions must take place in the dedicated Slack channel: #stellara-submission.
The team holds a mandatory daily sync meeting at 9:30 AM EST via Zoom link https://nit.zoom.us/j/9876543210.
Any change to one document that affects another must be announced in the #stellara-submission channel using the '@here' tag.
A master checklist for submission components is maintained as a Google Sheet named 'JAD Submission Checklist'.
Each component on the checklist requires a sign-off from its responsible owner and a final sign-off from Dr. Lena Petrova.
Dr. Aris Thorne is responsible for locking each document from further edits after Dr. Petrova's final approval is received.
Figure 3 in the manuscript, which shows simulation output, must be cross-referenced with the 'generate_figure_3.py' script in the code repository.
The number of data points cited in the manuscript's 'Methods' section (currently 1,482,910) must match the record count in the 'summary.txt' file within the final dataset.
All author affiliations must be listed exactly as 'Astrophysics Department, Northwood Institute of Technology, Meridian, CA 90210'.
